# 1.2.113 - Facilities and the Infiltrate tile: the Rest tile becomes Facilities, with a room's actions and five new Overflow states; Listen becomes Infiltrate, with Tail Someone, Dash, Shut the Door, Force the Door, Pick the Lock and Keep Watch, each rolled on the GMs' record; Repair the Lock as a project; a Reroll that replays the new rolls

Stages E93 (Facilities), E69 (the Infiltrate tile) and E74 (doors and Keep Watch), one release (the owner's decision of
12.11.2026), built on one work line from 1.2.105's line (f22a7e87), in that order. The commits:

- **E93**: C1 ee59a46, C6 5deb505, C3 afdc430, C2+C4 c0ad643, and later on the line the fix df3ffb6 (a fixture of an
  older test, E15-T4) and the room action's branch of E74 C7's Reroll replays (68ec08d).
- **E69**: C1 eba2b65, C2 5d2e2ab, C5 8b83fb8, the handbooks 2b5f594, the fix 33e5379, C3+C4 9b58219 and the fix
  68f8039, and later the Tail and Dash rows' drawings (a123ff1) and the Reroll's branches for a Dash and a tail (68ec08d).
- **E74**: C1+C2 f7d9fb2, C3 75aeb8d, C4 4f21e9e, C6 f64d5f6, d8905af, C5's Broken column 573ddad, the fix 32b4c1a, the
  glyphs a123ff1, C7 68ec08d, C5 e337ac9, 55dab3e, and the owner's answers of 12.11.2026 in 4780019.
- STATUS and notes commits with no code: 0590271, 97ef581, 80a8140, 3e8ea61, 40a920f, b00171f and those after
  4780019.

In plain words:

**E93, Facilities.**


- **The Facilities tile.** The tile that held Short Rest and Long Rest is named **Facilities** in English and Polish
  (its key stays `rest`). Inside it: the two rests, as before, and the actions of the room the character stands in.
- **A GM's room actions.** In Room Setup, the Rest tab is the **Facilities** tab: beside the two rest columns, a
  **Room actions** column with each room's count and an edit button. Each action has a name, a statistic, a
  difficulty and up to four effects (Health, Sanity, Hope, a search token, a Free Move, Hope for another present,
  minus the Overflow counter, text from the GM, a story effect, among others). A player's use is rolled: the roll is
  drawn on the primary GM's browser, its statistic the GMs' copy of the action's, and the effects are written there.
  A GM's action may be used by one person per time of day; once anyone uses it, a failed roll too, it is closed for
  everyone until the next time of day. Every use of a GM's action leaves a faint Subtle trace.
- **A completed project's action.** In the project manager, a button in a project's Edit cell (after the pen) sets
  the action a completed project gives: its name, its effects, whether it costs an action (default yes) and its
  lifetime (indefinite, or a number of days). It is offered in the project's room, with no roll, once per person per
  time of day. The Projects window's line of a completed project names its room action and the time left.
- **Five new Overflow states**, in Despair Flow's Overflow tab: **Lockdown** (room actions off for the time of day),
  **Insomnia** (no Short Rest), **Toll** (room actions cost one more action), **Jitters** (room action rolls at
  disadvantage) and **Power cut** (actions from completed projects off for the time of day). They start unticked:
  out of the hat until a GM ticks them (a default, below).

**E69, the Infiltrate tile.**


- **The Infiltrate tile.** The tile that held Listen is named **Infiltrate** in English and Polish (its key stays
  `listen`, no migration). It opens a window of rows, one row an action, each with its price: **Listen**, **Tail
  Someone** and **Dash** from E69, and E74's four below. Listen is greyed with its reason in a room
  with no neighbour; before, the warning came after the press.
- **Dash.** A Leg roll, drawn on the primary GM's browser; the GM grants the free crossings its band earns, off its own
  record of the roll.
- **Tail Someone.** Two rolls, both drawn on the GM: a Shadow roll against 15 decides whether the target learns of
  it (on a miss the target's owners are told the tailer's name at once), and the effect roll, Leg or Shadow, a GM's
  pick on the statistics card. The GM keeps the tail; each time the target's crossing settles, the tailer gets a
  card naming the room the target reached - live, in an Eclipse too. A critical effect roll names who stands in that
  room, outside an Eclipse only. One active tail per tailer, no daily limit. The tail ends when it is lost (the tailer
  stands in neither room at the target's settled crossing), at the day's end, at a body found, and when the target
  shakes it with a Dash (a Dash total above the tail's, or a critical; a critical tail only to a critical Dash);
  silently at a death or an incident.
- **A settled crossing**, `crossingSettled`: one event on the primary GM, scheduled from the GMs' record of every
  crossing, that the tail's cards (and the doors and Keep Watch, below) are read from.

**E74, the doors and Keep Watch.**


- **Shut the Door.** A Body roll, drawn on the primary GM's browser. In a room with at most two doors that open, not
  another's bedroom, not with a body the player knows of and nobody found, the GM keeps a barricade whose strength is
  the roll's total. A walk in through a door is refused on the walker's own browser and by the GMs' audit ("The door
  does not give."); a passage, a breach or a tunnel goes through, and a GM moving a token is never stopped. It comes
  down when its author leaves the room, at the time of day's end, at an Eclipse's start and at the season reset.
  Someone stopped at the door sends the barricade's author's owners a card, "Someone tries to get in", with no name,
  one card a barricade a quarter of a minute.
- **Force the Door.** A Body roll against everything that holds a door next to the character's room, all at once: a
  barricade by its strength (a tie holds), a GM's or a bedroom's lock and a seal at 18, a critical all. A forced lock
  stays broken until repaired; a forced seal is lifted for its time of day. The rooms next to either room hear a banging
  from it, with no name; the two rooms learn who it was; a bedroom's owner gets a card - on a pass, and on a miss with
  Despair.
- **Pick the Lock.** A Shadow roll against 16 for cover, then a Hand roll against 15 (18 clean), both drawn on the GM.
  At a door held by a lock or a seal (never a barricade) an open gives the picker a pass to the room beyond: they may
  walk in, by that door or another, and the pass lasts until they leave that room; one not used in its time of day is
  lost. Nobody is moved by it, and the lock stays locked for everyone else. The room beyond sees who it was below the
  cover; a bedroom's owner is warned of an open below 18 and of a miss with Despair.
- **Keep Watch.** A Body roll against 12, declared before an Eclipse (struck through in one and before the Night
  Eclipse). At the Eclipse's start the post is the watcher's room: a card of who is in it, a card for each settled
  crossing into or out of it (never which way), a summary at its end. The watcher is held to the post: a walk out of it
  in the Eclipse is put back by the primary GM. A miss with Despair marks a Sanity. A watch of 18 or more, or a
  critical, puts one hindrance die on the opening roll of whoever opens a murder on the watcher; that player's roll
  window names it "a hindrance die" ("kość utrudnienia") and never why.
- **Repair the Lock.** A project preset (Hand, Trivial), offered in Start New where a door of the builder's room has a
  broken lock, one project a door; its completion mends the lock. In Room Setup's Doors tab a **Broken** column shows a
  lock a Force or a breach broke; unticked and applied, the lock is mended.
- **Remnants.** A barricade leaves a subtle trace, a forced door an evident one where it was heard, a pick one by its
  roll (a miss with Despair evident, a miss with Hope and 15-17 subtle, 18 and over hidden).
- **A Reroll of these rolls** is replayed on the primary GM (until now a Reroll of any of them told the GMs "this roll
  left no lasting effect" and left the first result standing): a barricade's strength, a watch kept or let go, and a
  door forced or a lock picked by a higher roll, and a pass not yet used taken back by a lower one. A door forced, a pass
  the picker has used and a room action's effects stand when the new roll is lower, and the GMs' line says so.
- **The Infiltrate window** has its seven rows. Shut and Force wear different glyphs in both themes (Monokuma Legacy:
  Font Awesome's road barrier and fist; Stained Glass: E48's own drawings for the six rows).

Nothing in this version ran at a real table or on a Foundry server; what was measured was measured headless. Below,
an R number names one of the module's own tests (`game.drpg.runTests()`), and a scenario one of the headless
harness's multi-browser runs.

## Before installing

- **No world migration.** No clause was added to `migrate.mjs`, and no language key of the module's was removed or
  renamed. Two tiles change their label in both languages, their keys unchanged: Rest becomes **Facilities** (key
  `rest`; the rests' settings stay) and Listen becomes **Infiltrate** (key `listen`; Listen's approved description stays).
- **New stored data**: one world setting, `facilityClosed` (the GM's room actions closed for the time of day, by their
  key; `config: false`); six GM stores kept in the GMs' browsers, `facilityUses` (who used which room action and when),
  `tails` (who tails whom), `barricades` (strength, author), `watches` and `lockpicks` (the pick's passes), and each
  player's copy of their own characters' passes (`mineLockpicks`, a client setting their move veto reads); one public
  region flag, `ROOM_FLAGS.barricaded` (`true` and nothing else), on a barricaded room. That flag is held by every
  browser: a console reads which rooms are barricaded, never by whom or how strongly (the owner's DA47; Known gaps). A
  secret project's room action is kept in the GMs' half while the project is secret.
- **The Overflow hat**: the five new states are not drawn until a GM ticks them in Despair Flow. A table that changes
  nothing draws from the same states as before.
- **New bridge roads**: `facility.use`, `dash.settle`, `tail.start`, `door.shut`, `door.force`, `door.pick`,
  `watch.declare` and `door.knock`, each judged on the primary GM like every request of a player's browser. Two new
  refusal reasons, `barricaded` and `onWatch`, said to the player in their language. With no GM connected, none of the
  new actions can be taken, and nothing is paid. Two new GM-to-player socket packets, `lockpick.passes` (a GM's alone,
  taken only for the receiver's own characters) and its ask, `lockpick.passesAsk`.
- **The opening roll's invitation** (`murder.openingAsk`) may carry `hindrance: 1`, and nothing else of the watch. A
  browser on an older version ignores it and throws without the die; the GM's draw then names the difference to that
  player, as for any die the window left out, and throws its own.

## A Reroll of a Facilities roll (part of E74 C7, 68ec08d)

- Until 68ec08d, a Reroll of a room action's roll fell to reroll.mjs's `default`: the GMs were told "this roll left no
  lasting effect" and the first result stood. Now infiltrate-reroll.mjs `settleFacility` replays it on the primary GM
  from the facts the GMs' run wrote on the roll's row: a failure rerolled into a success applies the action's effects;
  a success stands (its effects were given), and the line says so.

  line; on the tree "6 passed". The numbers for the whole commit are in its own section below.

## A Reroll of a Dash or a tail (part of E74 C7, 68ec08d)

- Until 68ec08d, a Reroll of either fell to reroll.mjs's `default`: "this roll left no lasting effect", and the first
  result stood. Now infiltrate-reroll.mjs replays each on the primary GM from the facts the GMs' run wrote on the
  roll's row. A Dash: the new band's crossings granted up to it, or those still left taken down to it; spent ones are
  not taken back. A tail: its strength the new total and critical, where the tail still stands on the same target;
  otherwise the line says the tail is gone.
- Red first: E74-T6 and E74-T7 on a worktree of a123ff1 with only tests-tier2.mjs copied in, every case the no-replay
  line; on the tree "6 passed". The numbers for the whole commit are in its own section below.

## Known gaps

- **Not built**: the effects that need a mechanism the module does not have - an item's durability, a state removed,
  temporary +X to a trait, a temporary Experience, advantage on the next trait roll, a stronger next ultimate Hope Call,
  protection from Despair on a roll, a crossing in an Eclipse, project progress (it needs a pick of the project). No
  timed effect exists to extend. Q-E93-3 (the timed effects' length) is not reached.
- **No scenario of the stage's own**: scenario 33's E93-A, 30's forged packets and the tier-2 tests cover the roads.
- **Watched, not caught**: under Toll a GM's action costs 2 actions; the roller's browser pays both before the roll,
  and the GM's draw sees one payment, not its size. A console paying one under Toll rolls all the same.
- **A room's GM actions are region flags**, which every browser holds: a console reads them anywhere, the same as a
  room's description today.
- **Scenario 61's D5**, "the same browser back in world A reads its traces intact, and no GM had to send it a
  section": measured, not this line's code. Alone it passed 5 times of 5 on the line's last commit; two runs of 61 at
  once failed at that commit and at older ones of the line (f64d5f6 among them, which CI passed); at f22a7e87 one run
  alone passed. The section the GMs sent was the store `clockBeat`, the primary's periodic clock beat: when a beat
  lands while that browser is in world B, its copy of world A is one beat behind on its return.
- **Not in this release** (E69's own list): C6, the eavesdrop on LiveKit; C7, the Echoes; C8, the murder's privacy
  (its own stage, Q-E69-4's default); the GM handbook's section of the tile; E53's ledger counters (Q-E69-5).
- **A tail's card** names a room by its region name, even one the tailer never entered (a default, above).
- **The hindrance die tells the one who opens the murder that something hinders them.** Its cause is never sent (the invitation
  carries `hindrance: 1` and nothing else, E74-T10), but a die on the opening that the Night does not explain is itself
  a hint. That is the owner's option A.
- **A stale pass on a player's browser**: if a pass ends while its owner's browser is away, that browser's copy may
  still hold it until the primary answers its ask at the next load; its veto then lets a walk through that the GMs'
  audit sends back. Not measured headless as a reload; scenario 33 E74-C measures the copy updated while connected.
- **DA30's warning** to a bedroom's owner is sent at once, wherever the owner is, not at their next entry.
- **The barricade's public flag** (DA47) is the module's on purpose; its known-leaks row and README paragraph are
  not in this line's commits (proposed in docs/dev/e74/STATUS.md, "For the coordinator").
- **Not taken back by a lower Reroll**: a door forced, a pass the picker has already used, a room action's effects,
  and a Dash's crossings already spent. Each line says so.
- **Force the Door has no legal control in scenario 33** (Aiko's room in the harness has no neighbour); tier 2's E74-T2
  is its legal road, judged as the primary judges a player's packet.
- **E53's ledger counters** (Q-E74-5) are not in this release.
- **The look** was seen in Chromium on the harness's pages (audit/style-harness.html), both themes, EN and PL, at
  1366x768 and scale 2, in the review rounds of 12.11.2026: Facilities' window, Room Setup's Facilities tab and Doors tab,
  the two room-action editors, Despair Flow's Overflow tab, the project manager, the Infiltrate window with its seven rows,
  Tail Someone's, Force's and Pick's windows and Start New offering Repair the Lock. Not Foundry, no Font Awesome
  (Monokuma Legacy's rows show no icon there), no Foundry window frame; the cards and the roll window (with its "a
  hindrance die" line) are not drawn there. Seen and left as they are, each older than this line: the rests' sentence
  "No room on this map is marked for a yet" (an empty `{kind}`), and in Monokuma Legacy PL the Doors tab's headers
  "Zamknięte" and "Bez prywatności" cut in their narrow columns (already so at f22a7e87).
